questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose Lille university because of their academics subjects. They had a large different academic subjects which could give me some competences in differents fields that i wish working with in the future. So it was diffinitly for academic opportunities that i choose Lille university. Also i wanted to improve my french level, which i clearly has.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I will write about it later, but i give it 5, because i feel very inbetween about my stay here at Lille university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult. I think there is definitly a lack of information that wasn't clear at all. I think that the erasmus coordinaters did try to make it very clear, and they did as well in some areas. But for an exemple finding and making your sceduele was very unclear.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I think that they have been very good at helping at the university. But i still think there is an enorm lack of information in the beginning. During the semester they been very good at helping. But they need to organise or somehow make a "to do" in the beginnning at they stay, because it was overall very confusing. Also because when its confusing from the beginning you are already behind. And as a foreign your alwyas behind because of the language barrier, so having the organisation right it very important.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I rate it 3, because they have been excellent during the stay, but the beginning was not good at all.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Only residences which are far away from the city, but they have a nice big room. A large room with a bed, closet, table, chairs, kitchen and toilet.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a big kitchen on the first floor, and you also have a kitchen yourself which have everything you need, except a owen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That there can be bedbugs, i experienced it the first to months.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I give it three, because when i discovered bedbugs, it took them 1,5 months to find me another room, and they didn't help me find housing in the meantime. I am very lucky that i had a friend that i stayed at, but if not i dont know what i would have done. Very bad service.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did find it very difficult.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The day that all the french student started, you needed to "do your schedule", like choose with academic subjets that you wanted. You needed to go you around at the university to every departement to look at papers on the wall to see when/where the academic subjet took place. After that you needed to check on the internet how many ECTS it counted for. After that you needed to find every secretarie at the differents departments to tell them that you wanted to follow their subject. When you did that you also needed to contact every teacher and tell them that you were following their subects. They problem with all this is there is no one who tells you that you need to do this.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A bit, but not in the beginning which would have made it so much easier.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not so succesful. Actually even though we did tell them that we followed their sujects, we sometimes didn't get the emails because the teacher forgot to put us on their lists.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would offer future exchange student, to prepare for that it is going to be caotic in the beginning, and that they should just ask for help all the time. Dont hesistate.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They academic program i have choosen has been incrediable good. I have enjoyed it a lot, and i really think the teachers are fantastic.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 30 ECTS, the same as 30 UNITES.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think that the style of teaching here has been more creative in some ways, for an exemple i took a art class were we say old movies and anaysed them which i loved. But also more strict, for an exemple we did have to wait in front of the door befor the teacher came.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take just one art cours, they are really interessting and they teach it in a different way then in danmark.

questions.answer: I did get a friend who lived outside Lille (many who studies come from outside Lille), and it was quite expensive to visit him.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In my other fees DKK per month i have written 700 DK because i had a friend who lived outside Lille. But also some thing you have to have in mind is that when you go to a doctor you need to pay and then you need to apply to get the money back after. So that was quite expensive for me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are so many clubs, sports, events for exchange student here at Lille, it is a good place to be.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of sport, a cinema, language evening, taste cheese evenings etc. There is even just a restuarant for erasmus students. Also they arranged very cheap travels to all around in France.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitly to go on some of the trips, it is all arranged for you, and they are so cheap. In that way you get to see some of the country that you staying in.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Remember to check the local things out, for an exemple the museums etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, i think they have been very sweet down here. It has also been easy to get french friends as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take to some at the erasmus events at the beginning, but try also to talk to some of the french people in your class so you wont only become a part of the "erasmus society".

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They you go a lot out, it is very rare that you go home to someone.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the cheap food at university, the markets on every sunday and then they just live a bit more downhere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Be patient, learning agreement, papers to fill out is going to take some time and its okay
- Your erasmus grant can be slow to arrive, so make sure you have some money beside SU for your start. 
- In the beginning ask for all the help you need at the university, dont be shy.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to take dictionnaires with you, you wont be able to use your computer.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think that the courses has been the most rewarding part of my exchange experience, because they have been so interessting and giving. I feel like i have really improved my french level and at the same time my knowledge, and i feel a bit more clear about what i would like to do in the future.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the exams. I have had 12 exams which is a lot more then i Danmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
